title: Early arrangers: Leon Washington, Hicks, Sonny Blunt (Sun Ra)
summary: The small band used written arrangements by Leon Washington and a trumpeter named Hicks, while the show arranger was Sonny Blunt, later Sun Ra; the show changed every three weeks.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, let's go back to when you
first took over the band. You said it was a six-piece band.
Did you have written arrangements or --
Oh, yeah, we had everything then.

Well, we had two or three different people doing the writing then. Leon Washington wrote some for us, and then there was a fellow by the name of Hicks, trumpet player, and he was a very good arranger. So he wrote a lot of the things. See, the dance things and things like that.

And then, the show, they had their own arranger for the show. He would come in and rehearse with them, and then write a thing. What's his name was one of the guys that wrote -- I mean, put the music together, Sonny Blunt was his name, Sun Ra.
Yeah, right. Sonny Blunt was his name then. Then he changed, and --
How often would the show music change?
Every three weeks you'd have a new --
Right, now routines, everything, a new show.
